optionReasons.saa-ini-017:option:0: NACLs filtering network traffic into sub-networks — nothing to do with permissions from API or account governance.
optionReasons.saa-ini-017:option:2: Bucket policy controls access to a specific Bucket from S3 — does not restrict actions of the CloudTrail in multiple accounts.
optionReasons.saa-ini-017:option:3: Policies IAM act within UMA account and can be changed by local administrators — do not impose inviolable organizational limit.

finalJustifications: Because SCPs apply at the organisational level (OY/accounts) and define the ceiling of permissions — which is SCP nega gets blocked even for administrators.
Because the SCPs encrypt the tracks of the CloudTrail with an organization key, making exclusion impossible without access to the key.
Because the SCPs replace policies IAM within each OU account, centralizing the permissions granted to users.
Because the SCPs monitor the actions of the organization and automatically undo the exclusions detected in the unit accounts.

optionReasons.saa-ini-005:option:0: Creating VPCs is service operation Amazon VPC — is not health check function.
optionReasons.saa-ini-005:option:2: Managing policies IAM it is the function of the own IAM — without relation to health checks.
optionReasons.saa-ini-005:option:3: DNS is a public protocol by nature — the Route 53 does not encrypt records; data encryption is a KMS/TLS.

finalJustifications: Because health checks monitor the availability of endpoints and feed routing policies that divert traffic from unhealthy resources.
Because health checks scale the capacity of monitored servers when they detect degradation, anticipating unavailability.
Because health checks keep an automatic backup of records DNS, restoring the hosted area in case of undue alteration.
Because the health checks inspect the appointments DNS and block the DDoS attack patterns before they reach the endpoints.

optionReasons.saa-ini-023:option:0: The Direct Connect uses dedicated physical circuit that takes weeks to provide — does not meet the requirement of fast deployment via the internet.
optionReasons.saa-ini-023:option:1: Peering connects two VPCs inside the AWS — does not connect an on-premises office to a VPC.
optionReasons.saa-ini-023:option:3: The Route 53 solve names DNS — does not establish encrypted network tunnels.

finalJustifications: Because the Site-to-Site VPN creates encrypted IPsec tunnels via the Internet between the local gateway and the VPC, available in hours.
Because the VPN of AWS discover and configure the company router automatically, dispensing any change on the local side.
Because the Site-to-Site VPN offers dedicated and guaranteed band superior to that of Direct Connect, for using multiple tunnels in parallel.
Because the VPN encapsulates corporate traffic in HTTPS, dispensing IPsec and crossing any firewall without configuration.

optionReasons.saa-ini-001:option:0: User IAM is long-term identity with permanent credentials — not designed to be temporarily assumed by a service.
optionReasons.saa-ini-001:option:2: A policy defines permissions, but needs to be attached to an identity — it cannot itself be "assumed" to generate credentials.
optionReasons.saa-ini-001:option:3: Group IAM only groups users to apply policies together — cannot be assumed or generates temporary credentials.

finalJustifications: Because a Role is assumed by services or users and delivers temporary credentials with specific permissions, without sharing long-term secrets.
Because Role stores the passwords and keys of users with encryption of KMS, delivering them to the service at the time of access.
Because Role doubles the administrator's permissions to the authorized service, inheriting the account policies temporarily.
Because Role converts the user's permanent access keys into temporary credentials, rotating them at each session.

optionReasons.saa-ini-295:option:1: The DataSync MOVE data between on-premises and AWS in transfers — does not provide continuous hybrid access with local cache.
optionReasons.saa-ini-295:option:2: The EFS is a filesystem NFS native to AWS — does not keep the data in S3 neither offers local cache on-premises.
optionReasons.saa-ini-295:option:3: The Transfer Family exposes SFTP/FTPS managed on the S3 for partners — is not a local hybrid file server.

finalJustifications: Because File Gateway exposes a share NFS/SMB local, record the data as objects in S3 and keeps cached only the hot files.
Because File Gateway replicates the entire file server to the EFS, maintaining the NFS location as a share read replica.
Because File Gateway synchronizes local folders with the cloud for a VPN dedicated, scheduling shipments outside business hours.
Because File Gateway transforms the server NFS place in a pocket S3 physical, with the same API of objects available in the internal network.

optionReasons.saa-ini-012:option:0: The GuardDuty detects security threats (malice activity) — not underutilized resources for cost optimization.
optionReasons.saa-ini-012:option:1: The Route 53 It's DNS — does not analyze use of resources nor generates cost recommendations.
optionReasons.saa-ini-012:option:2: The Direct Connect is dedicated network connectivity — unrelated to identifying idle resources.

finalJustifications: Because Trusted Advisor analyzes the account and recommends optimizations in categories such as cost, pointing idle or underutilized resources.
Because Trusted Advisor automatically shut down the detected idle instances, applying cost optimizations without approval.
Because Trusted Advisor renegotiates prices with the AWS based on historical use, converting idleness into discounts in the invoice.
Because Trusted Advisor is the only service with access to metrics of CPU of the bodies, basis of the under-utilisation report.

optionReasons.saa-ini-009:option:1: Glacier Flexible Retrieval is archived with recovery from minutes to hours — not milliseconds.
optionReasons.saa-ini-009:option:2: Despite the name "Instant", this class is for ARQUIVAMENTO rarely accessed, with recovery rate — not for frequent access.
optionReasons.saa-ini-009:option:3: Deep Archive is the cheapest and slowest class (until 12 hours) — the opposite of frequent access.

finalJustifications: Because S3 Standard is designed for frequent access: millisecond latency, high transfer rate and no recovery rate.
Because S3 Standard records objects in unique NVMe SSDs per client, which ensures the latency of milliseconds in readings.
Because S3 Standard keeps the most accessible objects in memory RAM of servers, working as a managed cache.
Because S3 Standard is the only class that replicates objects between multiple AZs — the others keep a single local copy.

optionReasons.saa-ini-003:option:0: The CloudFormation provide infrastructure via templates (IaC) — does not automatically store or rotate secrets.
optionReasons.saa-ini-003:option:1: The Route 53 It's DNS and traffic routing — not related to credentials.
optionReasons.saa-ini-003:option:3: The S3 Glacier is low-cost archiving storage — does not manage secrets or rotate credentials.

finalJustifications: Because Secrets Manager storage, recovery and ROTACIONA secrets automatically, with native integration to RDS and other banks.
Because Secrets Manager encrypt each secret with a fixed and unchangeable key KMS, which ensures that the password never needs to change.
Because Secrets Manager inject passwords directly into the source code during build, eliminating calls from API in runtime.
Because Secrets Manager is free for any volume of secrets, being the economic alternative to Parameter Store.
